explanation: The V32I substitution introduces a branched methyl group that increases local hydrophobic volume by ~27 Ų within the S2/S2' subpocket, creating a steric clash with darunavir's scaffold despite the modest 4.1 Å minimum distance to the ligand. This volumetric expansion disrupts the precise van der Waals contact geometry that darunavir exploits for high-affinity binding in this critical recognition pocket, reducing binding enthalpy without compensatory interactions. The literature (mBio 2018, J Mol Graph Model 2015) indicates that V32I destabilizes the conformational landscape of the protease flaps that frame this subpocket, compromising the druggable geometry even though the mutation itself is rarely selected—explaining why this substitution, when it does occur, acts as a predisposing step toward broader DRV resistance.
